summary: beaver-ui-form postinstall dropper fetches and executes obfuscated binary from Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: beaver-ui-form@12.6.1 runs setup.js from both the package.json postinstall lifecycle hook and at require-time via index.js. setup.js selects a platform-specific asset path and fetches an unpinned, unverified native binary from Cloudflare Workers subdomains whose hostnames (oob-worker.cf*.workers.dev) are hidden via string-split array-join concatenation (e.g., ["oob-wor","ker.cf","99-9b3.wor","kers",".dev"]). The fetched bytes are written to a hidden path (/var/tmp/.cache_<rand> on POSIX, %TEMP%\dotnet_diag_<rand>.exe on Windows), chmod 0755, and launched detached via execFile; on Windows a powershell -nop -c irm branch is used. A DNS-TXT fallback channel under wel1.site reassembles base64 chunks from numbered subdomains (c.<domain>, 0.<domain>..n.<domain>) to reconstruct the binary when HTTPS is blocked. Cover-story naming ('.analytics_state', 'dotnet_diag_*.exe') and opt-out env-var gates (DISABLE_TELEMETRY, ANALYTICS_OPT_OUT, DO_NOT_TRACK) frame the behavior as telemetry, but the package advertises 'visual UI form components' with no legitimate need for a native binary. The drop-and-execute path fires automatically on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
